paper.title: On Multi-Armed Bandit Designs for Dose-Finding Clinical Trials

settings.name_in_paper: MTD identification as a bandit problem (minimizing sub-optimal dose allocations)
unmapped: Optimal arm is the arm whose mean is closest to a known target threshold theta (MTD), not the arm with largest mean
Performance measured by expected number of selections of each sub-optimal dose rather than regret
Learner knows the target toxicity threshold theta
settings.definition_quote: the Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD) is defined as the dose with a toxicity probability closest to a target: k^* \in argmin_k |\theta - p_k| ... We assume that X_t is drawn from a Bernoulli distribution with mean p_{D_t} ... this second objective can be formalized as that of minimizing N_k(n) for k\neq k^*.

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-budget MTD identification (variant of fixed-budget best arm identification)

settings.definition_quote: Minimizing the error probability for MTD can be viewed as a variant of the fixed-budget Best Arm Identification (BAI) problem ... the focus is on identifying the arm whose mean is closest to the threshold \theta.

algorithms.name: Independent Thompson Sampling (uniform Beta priors, MTD selection)

symbols.d_k_star: argmin over d in {p_{k*}, 2 theta - p_{k*}} of |p_k - d|
symbols.C_eps: constant depending on epsilon, threshold theta and toxicity probabilities p

source.label: thm:TS
source.quote: Introducing for every $k\neq k^*$ the quantity $d_k^* := \argmin{d \in \{p_{k^*},2\theta - p_{k^*}\}} |p_k - d |$, Independent Thompson Sampling satisfies the following. For all $\varepsilon >0$, there exists a constant $C_{\varepsilon,\theta,\bm p}$ ... such that for all $k : |p_k - \theta| \neq |\theta - p_{k^*}|$, $\bE[N_{k}(n)] \leq \frac{1 + \varepsilon}{\mathrm{kl}(p_k,d_k^*)} \log(n) + C_{\varepsilon,\theta,\bm p}$

results.notes: Bound on expected number of selections of a sub-optimal dose (quantity 'other'). Optimal arm is the dose closest to threshold theta. The paper derives P(k_hat_n != k*) <= D ln(n)/n as a consequence (not recorded separately).

symbols.d_k_star: argmin over d in {p_{k*}, 2 theta - p_{k*}} of |p_k - d|

results.notes: Lai-Robbins-type lower bound on sub-optimal dose allocations, matched by Theorem 1.

symbols.H_2: H_2(p) = max_{k != k*} k * Delta_[k]^{-2}, with Delta_k = |p_k - theta| - |p_{k*} - theta| sorted increasingly

source.label: thm:SH
source.quote: The error probability of the \texttt{SH} algorithm is upper bounded as $\bP\left(\hat{k}_n \neq k^*\right) \leq 9 \log_2 K \cdot \exp \left( - \frac{n}{8 H_2 (\bm p)\log_2 K} \right)$, where $H_2(\bm p):= \max_{k \ne k^*} {k}{\Delta_{[k]}^{-2}}$ where $\Delta_k = |p_k - \theta| - |p_{k^*} - \theta|$ and $\Delta_{[1]} \leq \Delta_{[2]} \leq \dots \leq \Delta_{[K]}$.

results.notes: Error probability bound; 'probability' field set to high_probability as closest option for an error-probability statement. The proof's Lemma 7 uses Delta_k^2 = min{(p_k-p_{k*})^2, (p_k-(2theta-p_{k*}))^2}, slightly differing from the stated Delta_k definition.
